title: EXP-061 — Hello World Part 4 Section 3: Add and Recover FX_Picture Bound Property on FX_Items IDO
objective: Using the existing authenticated Mongoose Web Client, open the native IDO Collections runtime maintenance Form through Open > Select Form. Retrieve exactly FX_Items and establish its project, base table, revision, checkout ownership, and complete existing property inventory. Prove that the FX_Picture IDO property is absent and verify that the existing dbo.FX_Items.FX_Picture column and FX_Picture Binary property class are available. If FX_Items is checked in, perform exactly one native checkout of FX_Items; if already checked out to the current operator, perform no checkout. Using the native New Property wizard, add exactly one property named FX_Picture, retain the default Bound property type, bind it to the existing FX_Picture SQL column, and select the existing FX_Picture property class. Verify the wizard's inherited data type and SQL column type, invoke Finish exactly once, and perform at most one ordinary toolbar Save if required. Close the clean IDO Collections Form once, reopen it once, and retrieve FX_Items to verify that the property inventory equals the original baseline plus exactly one FX_Picture property with the correct binding and class. Confirm that FX_Items remains checked out to the current operator. Finally, open the existing FX_Items runtime Form read-only and verify that its three pre-existing records still load. Capture native evidence, complete the action audit, and classify the result observed only.

Configure the new IDO Property Name as FX_Picture and select the existing FX_Picture property class through supported native controls.
Read and record the Data Type and SQL Column Data Type displayed or inherited by the wizard. Require compatible Binary and varbinary semantics and no unexpected conversion.

Verify one and only one FX_Picture property on FX_Items, with Property Type Bound, bound column FX_Picture, and property class FX_Picture. Confirm that the original property inventory is otherwise unchanged.
Verify the IDO remains checked out to the current operator and record its revision and ownership after the property addition.

Compare the recovered inventory against the pre-change baseline, requiring exactly one added FX_Picture property and no other property additions, removals, or changes.
Open the existing FX_Items runtime Form once through the supported native route. Read-only verification must establish that the same three pre-existing records still load and the Form remains clean.
Leave the FX_Items IDO checked out to the current operator. Leave all other objects and inherited browser tabs unchanged.

Capture decisive screenshots and accessibility readbacks under evidence/EXP-061/, including target identity, baseline inventory, checkout, wizard configuration, Finish and Save responses, post-change state, close/reopen, recovered property inventory, ownership, and three-record runtime verification.
Use one fresh untargeted snapshot and at most one corrected visible inspection following a locator or visibility failure. If unresolved, record a blocker rather than expanding the procedure.

acceptance_checks.description: Required AGENTS.md, tutorial Section 3, and related experiment records were reviewed. Starting repository state was documented. The existing authenticated Web Client is usable, and the native IDO Collections maintenance Form opens through Open > Select Form without authentication or session challenges. Evidence: source-review notes, configuration/identity screenshot, native maintenance heading, initial Form screenshot, and action audit.

One initial native exact-name query retrieves exactly one FX_Items IDO. Its IDO project, base table, revision, current checkout status, Locked By owner, and complete pre-change property inventory are recorded. The inventory visibly establishes that FX_Picture is absent and contains no ambiguous or duplicate target. Evidence: exact query screenshot, target header, complete inventory screenshots/readbacks, property count, and baseline matrix. If absence or identity cannot be established, no mutation occurs.

The native UI confirms that the existing dbo.FX_Items.FX_Picture SQL column is available and compatible with a binary binding. The existing FX_Picture property class is identified unambiguously and is available for selection. Evidence: native column and class identity, visible type information, and lookup readbacks. Missing or incompatible prerequisites block mutation.

The FX_Items checkout prerequisite is satisfied without violating ownership boundaries. If already checked out to the current operator, zero checkout actions occur. Otherwise exactly one authorized native checkout of FX_Items occurs, with any response recorded verbatim and resulting Locked By matching the operator. No other object is checked out, and no check-in or undo-checkout operation occurs. Evidence: before/after ownership screenshots, revision readback, and checkout-action audit.

Exactly one native New Property wizard is configured for the FX_Items IDO with Property Name FX_Picture, Property Type Bound, Bind To FX_Picture, and Property Class FX_Picture. The wizard's inherited data type and SQL column type are visibly captured and compatible with Binary and varbinary. Every selection is committed and verified before exactly one Finish. Evidence: full pre-Finish wizard screenshots, accessibility readbacks, property/class/column identity, Finish count, and verbatim native response.

After Finish and at most one ordinary Save if required, IDO Collections is clean with Save disabled and no unresolved error or consequential confirmation. Exactly one FX_Picture property is present with Bound type, FX_Picture column binding, and FX_Picture property class. All original FX_Items properties and their recorded attributes are unchanged. FX_Items remains checked out to the current operator. Evidence: Save/Finish response, settled Form screenshot, post-change inventory, ownership readback, and baseline-plus-one comparison.

The clean IDO Collections internal Form is closed exactly once without an unsaved-changes prompt and reopened exactly once through Open > Select Form. One native post-reopen exact-name query retrieves FX_Items. The recovered property inventory equals the original baseline plus exactly one Bound FX_Picture property connected to column FX_Picture and class FX_Picture; original properties are unchanged. The IDO remains checked out to the current operator, and Save is disabled. Evidence: close/reopen screenshots, recovered identity, complete property inventory, field-by-field comparison, revision, and Locked By.

The existing FX_Items runtime Form opens read-only through a supported native route and loads the same three pre-existing records. The Form remains clean, with no business-record modification, and no picture component or runtime image functionality is claimed. Evidence: FX_Items Form identity, three-record rendered grid or count with identifiable rows, Save-disabled state, and action audit.

A cumulative action audit proves exactly one property-wizard initiation, one Finish, zero or one ordinary Save as required, zero or one authorized FX_Items checkout, one IDO Collections close, one reopen, and one post-reopen recovery query. No additional IDO/property, SQL object, property class, Form definition, or business record was modified. No check-in, undo checkout, unload, diagnostic, script, or unauthorized operation occurred. Worker-written inventories and harness audits support repository confinement, with authoritative final git review reserved for the operator. Evidence: task-level action tables, harness tool audits, written-file inventory, and explicit limitations.

The final EXP-061 report contains decisive evidence references for AC-1 through AC-9, the complete original and recovered property inventories, SQL column/class prerequisites, wizard values, inherited types, Finish and Save responses, checkout ownership, exact action counts, runtime three-row result, final Form state, blockers, and repository audit. Findings are classified observed only. Independent database durability, cross-session recovery, automatic cache invalidation, replay verification, and PNG runtime functionality are not claimed. Evidence: final report under evidence/EXP-061/ and completed EXP-061 experiment record.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261011-215916-hvC7. Rationale: EXP-060 accepted the native creation, Save, and close/reopen recovery of the FX_Picture Binary property class with Length -1, Column Data Type varbinary, and Binary Format PNG. EXP-059 targeted the corresponding nullable FX_Picture SQL column on dbo.FX_Items, while EXP-049 established the factory-owned FX_Items IDO. The next tutorial step at 02:13–03:00 is to connect these existing objects by adding exactly one bound property to FX_Items. This experiment introduces one new capability: native IDO property addition and recovery through IDO Collections. It uses the operator's explicit authorization to check out FX_Items once if required and leave it checked out. Because the available EXP-059 status summary is incomplete, the SQL column must be verified in the live native UI before mutation. No database, property-class, Form-definition, or business-record change is permitted. Results will be classified observed only. | Operator review 2026-10-11: checkout pattern now requires check out + another object (a mention of checkout state near "property class" no longer matches); exact_values FX_Items, FX_Picture; deny_browser_javascript; editing scope. Operator decision 2026-10-11 ("continue, leave checked out"): one Check Out of the FX_Items IDO is authorized if required, and it stays checked out; no Check In, no Undo Check Out, no unload. Approval pending from the operator.
